newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo discount rate, reserve requirement unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Yugo discount rate, reserve requirement unchanged.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank kept its key discount rate for December unchanged at 4.5 percent per month to stave off possible monetary pressures building ahead of the year-end, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.

"December is usually a turbulent and unpredictable month. Activity on our financial market tends to intensify and becomes inflated towards the end of the year," the central bank Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic told Reuters.
Banovic said that the discount rate could have been reduced due to easing price pressures in November.

"But keeping the discount rate unchanged is only a precautionary measure to avert increasing pressures on the dinar exchange rate. Besides, we want to keep investor interest in our securities," Banovic said.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) sets the discount rate each month using a basket that includes interest rates on the open money market, its short-term bonds, price rises, expected monetary developments, credit demand and money supply.
The discount rate is said to be the key NBY's instrument in regulating market liquidity.
December was the seventh consecutive month that the discount rate was kept unchanged at an annual 68.15 percent.
The discount rate was first cut to 4.5 percent in June from 6.31 in May in an attempt to influence commercial lending rates down, but the reduction in lending rates failed to materialise.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) also left the reserve requirement unchanged at 15 percent, Banovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
